# 1 Clement Chapter 19 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 19 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_019_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 19

**19:1** The humility and humble submission of so many men of such repute — who have received attestation — has made better not only us, but also the generations before us, who received his oracles in fear and truth.

**19:2** Seeing therefore that we have a part in many great and glorious deeds, let us hasten to return to the goal of peace which was handed down to us from the beginning, and let us look to the Father and Maker of the whole world, and hold fast to his magnificent and surpassing gifts of peace and kindness.

**19:3** Let us look upon him with the eyes of our mind; let us consider his long-suffering will; let us reflect on how free from anger he is toward all his creation.

---

*EMET: "goal of peace" (*skopos tēs eirēnēs*) — peace is the target, the telos, of the entire exhortation. "Father and Maker of the whole world" — one of the earliest expressions of God as universal Father-Creator in a non-Jewish letter.*
